question: Which behavior defines streaming telemetry as a push model in Cisco devices?
options: Events and network changes generate telemetry data.
Monitoring clients are pulling data from the network to see real-time statistics.
JSON encoded telemetry data is transported using the gRPC protocol.
The network devices send data in JSON or GPB format to configure endpoints.
theory: Streaming telemetry is described as a "push" model because the network device itself initiates data delivery whenever relevant events or state changes occur (or on a defined cadence), sending it unprompted to a subscribed collector — the opposite of a pull model where a client must first request data. That event/change-driven, device-initiated delivery (rather than encoding format or transport protocol details) is what defines the push behavior. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Streaming Telemetry)
